sleep_ikhlas.title: Surah Al-Ikhlas (The Sincerity) — 1st of the Three Quls
sleep_ikhlas.arabicText: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ۔ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ۔ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ۔ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
sleep_ikhlas.transliteration: Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad. Allāhu aṣ-ṣamad. Lam yalid wa lam yūlad. Wa lam yakun lahū kufuwan aḥad.
sleep_ikhlas.translation: Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born. Nor is there to Him any equivalent.
sleep_ikhlas.benefit: Recite this into your cupped hands, blow gently into them, then wipe as much of your body as you can reach, beginning with the head and face, repeating the whole process three times before sleeping.
sleep_ikhlas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 9/62; Muslim 4/1723 | Hisnul Muslim 99

sleep_falaq.title: Surah Al-Falaq (The Daybreak) — 2nd of the Three Quls
sleep_falaq.arabicText: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ۔ مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ۔ وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ۔ وَمِن شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ۔ وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
sleep_falaq.transliteration: Qul a'ūdhu bi-rabb al-falaq. Min sharri mā khalaq. Wa min sharri ghāsiqin idhā waqab. Wa min sharri an-naffāthāti fī al-'uqad. Wa min sharri ḥāsidin idhā ḥasad.
sleep_falaq.translation: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of that which He created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles, and from the evil of the blowers in knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies.
sleep_falaq.benefit: Recited together with Al-Ikhlas and An-Nas into the cupped hands, then blown upon and wiped over the body three times before sleeping, for protection through the night.
sleep_falaq.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 9/62; Muslim 4/1723 | Hisnul Muslim 99

sleep_nas.title: Surah An-Nas (Mankind) — 3rd of the Three Quls
sleep_nas.arabicText: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ۔ مَلِكِ النَّاسِ۔ إِلَهِ النَّاسِ۔ مِن شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ۔ الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ۔ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ
sleep_nas.transliteration: Qul a'ūdhu bi-rabb an-nās. Malik an-nās. Ilāh an-nās. Min sharri al-waswāsi al-khannās. Alladhī yuwaswisu fī ṣudūr an-nās. Min al-jinnati wa an-nās.
sleep_nas.translation: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the Sovereign of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer, who whispers in the breasts of mankind, from among jinn and mankind.
sleep_nas.benefit: The final of the Three Quls, recited into the cupped hands, blown upon, and wiped over the body three times before sleeping, completing the Prophet's nightly protection.
sleep_nas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 9/62; Muslim 4/1723 | Hisnul Muslim 99

sleep_ayatul_kursi.title: Ayatul Kursi (The Verse of the Throne)
sleep_ayatul_kursi.arabicText: اَللّٰهُ لَاۤ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا هُوَۚ اَلۡحَیُّ الۡقَیُّوۡمُ ۬ۚ لَا تَاۡخُذُهٗ سِنَۃٌ وَّ لَا نَوۡمٌ ؕ لَهٗ مَا فِی السَّمٰوٰتِ وَ مَا فِی الۡاَرۡضِ ؕ مَنۡ ذَا الَّذِیۡ یَشۡفَعُ عِنۡدَهٗۤ اِلَّا بِاِذۡنِهٖ ؕ یَعۡلَمُ مَا بَیۡنَ اَیۡدِیۡهِمۡ وَ مَا خَلۡفَهُمۡ ۚ وَ لَا یُحِیۡطُوۡنَ بِشَیۡءٍ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهٖۤ اِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِیُّهُ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَ الۡاَرۡضَ ۚ وَ لَا یَـُٔوۡدُهٗ حِفۡظُهُمَا ۚ وَ هُوَ الۡعَلِیُّ الۡعَظِیۡمُ
sleep_ayatul_kursi.transliteration: Allāhu lā ilāha illā huw, al-ḥayyu al-qayyūm, lā ta'khudhuhū sinatun wa lā nawm, lahū mā fī as-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ, man dhā alladhī yashfa'u 'indahū illā bi-idhnih, ya'lamu mā bayna aydīhim wa mā khalfahum, wa lā yuḥīṭūna bi-shay'in min 'ilmihī illā bimā shā'a, wasi'a kursiyyuhū as-samāwāti wa al-arḍa, wa lā ya'ūduhū ḥifẓuhumā, wa huwa al-'aliyyu al-'aẓīm.
sleep_ayatul_kursi.translation: Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
sleep_ayatul_kursi.benefit: Whoever recites this when lying down to sleep will have a guardian from Allah remain with him, and Satan will not be able to approach him until he wakes in the morning.
sleep_ayatul_kursi.reference: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:255. Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 4/487 | Hisnul Muslim 100

sleep_last_two_ayat_baqarah.title: The Last Two Verses of Surah Al-Baqarah
sleep_last_two_ayat_baqarah.arabicText: ءَامَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِن رَّبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّن رُّسُلِهِ وَقَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ {285} لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِن نَّسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا أَنتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ {286}
sleep_last_two_ayat_baqarah.transliteration: Āmanar-Rasūlu bimā unzila ilaihi mir-Rabbihi wa al-mu'minūn. Kullun āmana billāhi wa malā'ikatihi wa kutubihi wa rusulih. Lā nufarriqu bayna aḥadim-mir-rusulih. Wa qālū sami'nā wa aṭa'nā, ghufrānaka Rabbanā wa ilayka al-maṣīr. Lā yukallifu Allāhu nafsan illā wus'ahā. Lahā mā kasabat wa 'alayhā mak-tasabat. Rabbanā lā tu'ākhidhnā in nasīnā aw akhṭa'nā. Rabbanā wa lā taḥmil 'alaynā iṣran kamā ḥamaltahu 'alal-ladhīna min qablinā. Rabbanā wa lā tuḥammilnā mā lā ṭāqata lanā bih. Wa'fu 'annā, waghfir lanā, warḥamnā. Anta mawlānā fanṣurnā 'alā al-qawmi al-kāfirīn.
sleep_last_two_ayat_baqarah.translation: The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His Messengers. They say: 'We make no distinction between any of His Messengers,' and: 'We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the return.' Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear. It will have what it earns, and it will bear what it deserves. Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with more than we have strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people.
sleep_last_two_ayat_baqarah.benefit: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said these two verses will be sufficient for anyone who recites them at night.
sleep_last_two_ayat_baqarah.reference: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:285-286. Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 9/94; Muslim 1/554 | Hisnul Muslim 101

sleep_bismika_wadatu_janbi.title: Bismika Rabbi Wada'tu Janbi (In Your Name I Lay Myself Down)
sleep_bismika_wadatu_janbi.arabicText: بِاسْمِكَ رَبِّي وَضَعْتُ جَنْبِي وَبِكَ أَرْفَعُهُ فَإِنْ أَمْسَكْتَ نَفْسِي فَارْحَمْهَا وَإِنْ أَرْسَلْتَهَا فَاحْفَظْهَا بِمَا تَحْفَظُ بِهِ عِبَادَكَ الصَّالِحِينَ
sleep_bismika_wadatu_janbi.transliteration: Bismika Rabbī waḍa'tu janbī, wa bika arfa'uh. Fa in amsakta nafsī farḥamhā, wa in arsaltahā faḥfaẓhā bimā taḥfaẓu bihi 'ibādakaṣ-ṣāliḥīn.
sleep_bismika_wadatu_janbi.translation: With Your Name, my Lord, I lay myself down, and with Your Name I rise. If You take my soul, then have mercy on it, and if You send it back, then protect it as You protect Your righteous slaves.
sleep_bismika_wadatu_janbi.benefit: Recited upon lying down for sleep, after dusting off the bed three times, entrusting one's soul to Allah whether it is taken in sleep or returned come morning.

sleep_allahumma_khalaqta_nafsi.title: Allahumma Innaka Khalaqta Nafsi (O Allah, You Created My Soul)
sleep_allahumma_khalaqta_nafsi.arabicText: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ خَلَقْتَ نَفْسِي وَأَنْتَ تَوَفَّاهَا لَكَ مَمَاتُهَا وَمَحْيَاهَا إِنْ أَحْيَيْتَهَا فَاحْفَظْهَا وَإِنْ أَمَتَّهَا فَاغْفِرْ لَهَا اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَافِيَةَ
sleep_allahumma_khalaqta_nafsi.transliteration: Allāhumma innaka khalaqta nafsī wa anta tawaffāhā, laka mamātuhā wa maḥyāhā. In aḥyaytahā faḥfaẓhā, wa in amattahā faghfir lahā. Allāhumma innī as'aluka al-'āfiyah.
sleep_allahumma_khalaqta_nafsi.translation: O Allah, You have created my soul and You take it back. Unto You belongs its death and its life. If You give it life, then protect it, and if You cause it to die, then forgive it. O Allah, I ask You for well-being.
sleep_allahumma_khalaqta_nafsi.benefit: An acknowledgment before sleeping that Allah alone owns one's life and death, closing with a request for well-being in both.

sleep_allahumma_qini_adhabaka.title: Allahumma Qini Adhabak (O Allah, Save Me from Your Punishment)
sleep_allahumma_qini_adhabaka.arabicText: اللَّهُمَّ قِنِي عَذَابَكَ يَوْمَ تَبْعَثُ عِبَادَكَ
sleep_allahumma_qini_adhabaka.translation: O Allah, save me from Your punishment on the Day that You resurrect Your slaves.
sleep_allahumma_qini_adhabaka.benefit: The Prophet (peace be upon him) would place his right hand under his cheek before sleeping and say this short supplication seeking safety on the Day of Judgment.
sleep_allahumma_qini_adhabaka.reference: Abu Dawud 4/311; Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/143 | Hisnul Muslim 104

sleep_bismika_amutu_wa_ahya.title: Bismika Allahumma Amutu wa Ahya (In Your Name I Die and Live)
sleep_bismika_amutu_wa_ahya.translation: In Your Name, O Allah, I die and I live.
sleep_bismika_amutu_wa_ahya.benefit: A brief remembrance recited before sleeping, likening sleep to death and waking to life, both entrusted entirely to Allah's Name.
sleep_bismika_amutu_wa_ahya.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 11/113; Muslim 4/2083 | Hisnul Muslim 105

sleep_tasbih_fatimi.title: Tasbih Fatimi (33x Subhanallah, 33x Alhamdulillah, 34x Allahu Akbar)
sleep_tasbih_fatimi.arabicText: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ (ثَلَاثاً وَثَلَاثِينَ) وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ (ثَلَاثاً وَثَلَاثِينَ) وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ (أَرْبَعاً وَثَلَاثِينَ)
sleep_tasbih_fatimi.transliteration: Subḥānallāh (33 times). Wal-ḥamdu lillāh (33 times). Wallāhu akbar (34 times).
sleep_tasbih_fatimi.translation: Glory be to Allah (33 times), praise be to Allah (33 times), and Allah is the Greatest (34 times). Recite in this sequence when taking to your bed.
sleep_tasbih_fatimi.benefit: The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught this tasbih to his daughter Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her) before sleeping, telling her it was better for her than a servant.
sleep_tasbih_fatimi.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 7/71; Muslim 4/2091 | Hisnul Muslim 106

sleep_allahumma_rabbas_samawati.title: Allahumma Rabbas-Samawatis-Sab' (O Allah, Lord of the Seven Heavens)
sleep_allahumma_rabbas_samawati.arabicText: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ السَّبْعِ وَرَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ رَبَّنَا وَرَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَالِقَ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَى وَمُنَزِّلَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ وَالْفُرْقَانِ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ أَنْتَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهِ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الْأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَكَ شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَكَ شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَكَ شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَكَ شَيْءٌ اقْضِ عَنَّا الدَّيْنَ وَأَغْنِنَا مِنَ الْفَقْرِ
sleep_allahumma_rabbas_samawati.transliteration: Allāhumma Rabbas-samāwātis-sab'i wa Rabba al-'Arshi al-'Aẓīm. Rabbanā wa Rabba kulli shay', fāliqa al-ḥabbi wan-nawā, wa munzilat-Tawrāti wal-Injīli wal-Furqān. A'ūdhu bika min sharri kulli shay'in anta ākhidhun bināṣiyatih. Allāhumma anta al-awwalu falaysa qablaka shay', wa anta al-ākhiru falaysa ba'daka shay', wa anta aẓ-ẓāhiru falaysa fawqaka shay', wa anta al-bāṭinu falaysa dūnaka shay'. Iqḍi 'annad-dayn, wa aghninā minal-faqr.
sleep_allahumma_rabbas_samawati.translation: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Magnificent Throne, our Lord and the Lord of all things, Splitter of the grain and the date-stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion (the Quran), I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything You shall seize by the forelock. O Allah, You are the First, so nothing is before You, and You are the Last, so nothing is after You. You are the Most High, so nothing is above You, and You are the Most Near, so nothing is nearer than You. Settle our debts for us and spare us from poverty.
sleep_allahumma_rabbas_samawati.benefit: A comprehensive supplication recognizing Allah's total sovereignty over creation, seeking refuge from every evil, and asking relief from debt and poverty.

sleep_alhamdulillah_atamana.title: Alhamdulillahil-ladhi At'amana (Praise for Food, Drink and Shelter)
sleep_alhamdulillah_atamana.arabicText: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَكَفَانَا وَآوَانَا فَكَمْ مِمَّنْ لَا كَافِيَ لَهُ وَلَا مُؤْوِيَ
sleep_alhamdulillah_atamana.transliteration: Alḥamdu lillāhil-ladhī aṭ'amanā wa saqānā, wa kafānā, wa āwānā, fakam mimman lā kāfiya lahu wa lā mu'wī.
sleep_alhamdulillah_atamana.translation: Praise is to Allah, Who has fed us and given us drink, and has been sufficient for us and sheltered us, for how many are there who have no one to suffice them and no home.
sleep_alhamdulillah_atamana.benefit: A grateful acknowledgment before sleeping of Allah's provision of food, drink, and shelter — blessings many people go without.

sleep_allahumma_alimal_ghaybi.title: Allahumma 'Alimal-Ghaybi wash-Shahadah (O Allah, Knower of the Unseen)
sleep_allahumma_alimal_ghaybi.arabicText: اللَّهُمَّ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ رَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيكَهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ نَفْسِي وَمِنْ شَرِّ الشَّيْطَانِ وَشِرْكِهِ وَأَنْ أَقْتَرِفَ عَلَى نَفْسِي سُوءاً أَوْ أَجُرَّهُ إِلَى مُسْلِمٍ
sleep_allahumma_alimal_ghaybi.transliteration: Allāhumma 'ālimal-ghaybi wash-shahādah, fāṭiras-samāwāti wal-arḍ, Rabba kulli shay'in wa malīkah, ash-hadu an lā ilāha illā ant. A'ūdhu bika min sharri nafsī, wa min sharrish-shayṭāni wa shirkih, wa an aqtarifa 'alā nafsī sū'an aw ajurrahu ilā Muslim.
sleep_allahumma_alimal_ghaybi.translation: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Maker of the heavens and the earth, Lord of all things and their Sovereign, I bear witness that there is no deity except You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul, and from the evil of Satan and his helpers, and from bringing evil upon myself or drawing it upon any Muslim.
sleep_allahumma_alimal_ghaybi.benefit: A protective testimony of faith recited before sleeping, seeking refuge from the evil of one's own soul, Satan, and his helpers.
sleep_allahumma_alimal_ghaybi.reference: Abu Dawud 4/317; Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/142 | Hisnul Muslim 109

sleep_allahumma_aslamtu_nafsi.title: Allahumma Aslamtu Nafsi Ilayk (O Allah, I Submit Myself to You)
sleep_allahumma_aslamtu_nafsi.arabicText: اللَّهُمَّ أَسْلَمْتُ نَفْسِي إِلَيْكَ وَفَوَّضْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ وَوَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ وَأَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَيْكَ رَغْبَةً وَرَهْبَةً إِلَيْكَ لَا مَلْجَأَ وَلَا مَنْجَا مِنْكَ إِلَّا إِلَيْكَ آمَنْتُ بِكِتَابِكَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْتَ وَبِنَبِيِّكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ
sleep_allahumma_aslamtu_nafsi.transliteration: Allāhumma aslamtu nafsī ilayk, wa fawwaḍtu amrī ilayk, wa wajjahtu wajhī ilayk, wa alja'tu ẓahrī ilayk, raghbatan wa rahbatan ilayk. Lā malja'a wa lā manjā minka illā ilayk. Āmantu bikitābika al-ladhī anzalt, wa bi-nabiyyika al-ladhī arsalt.
sleep_allahumma_aslamtu_nafsi.translation: O Allah, I submit myself to You, I entrust my affairs to You, I turn my face to You, and I lay myself down depending upon You, in hope and in fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. I believe in Your Book that You revealed, and in Your Prophet whom You sent.
sleep_allahumma_aslamtu_nafsi.benefit: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said whoever recites this after performing ablution and lying on their right side, and dies that night, dies upon the natural state of pure faith (fitrah).
sleep_allahumma_aslamtu_nafsi.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 11/113; Muslim 4/2081 | Hisnul Muslim 111
